Subject: APAC node sizing - initial ask

Hi Neha,

We're finalizing the SOW for our pilot in Singapore and need Redwood's recommendation on a node mix and a warm-standby strategy. Key constraints:
- Target steady-state qps: 120k tokens/day for generation workloads, peak bursts up to 2.5M tokens/day for short windows.
- Latency SLO: 120ms p95 for 1-2k concurrent requests.
- Data residency: logs and KV cache must remain in APAC (Singapore) for audit reasons.
- Procurement window: we'd like activation within 6 weeks of signature.

Questions: can you propose a draft node mix (H100 vs A100, reserved vs burst), and an activation plan that meets the 6-week target while limiting upfront committed cost? Also please flag any compliance or procurement blockers.

Thanks,
Maria

Subject: Re: Fwd: APAC node sizing - OrbitAI (draft sizing attached)

Neha — attached a first-pass sizing workbook (sizing-runbook.xlsx). Key assumptions and tradeoffs:
- Model: LLM-XX-16B, FP16 runtime. Baseline token throughput per H100 node ~ 350k tokens/hr steady; A100 ~ 220k tokens/hr.
- Steady-state (120k tokens/day) is tiny relative to capacity; design driven by burst windows and p95 latency.

Proposal (short):
- Reserved pool: 2 x H100 nodes (primary), 2 x A100 nodes (hot spare) — covers baseline + sustained bursts up to ~1M tokens/day with preserved latency.
- Warm-standby burst pool (on-demand/hybrid): 4 x H100 spot-capable nodes with pre-pulled images and cached weights/KV. These are not fully committed but can be spun from reserved capacity or cloud-burst in ~30-90 mins depending on availability.
- KV cache placement: cache pinned to local NVMe on SG nodes; use prefix cache snapshotting to S3 in-region every 15 minutes for quick rehydrate on spin-up.

Activation path to 6 weeks:
- Week 0-1: confirm MOA and model config; procurement reserve order for 2 H100 and 2 A100.
- Week 2-3: infra provisioning, kernel selection, and pre-warm images + cache seeding using sample data.
- Week 4: internal performance runbook and canary traffic.
- Week 5-6: customer acceptance testing and SLO signoff.

Risks: H100 allocation lead time could be the gating item. If H100s delay beyond 4 weeks, fallback is to deploy 4x A100 reserved + 2 H100 burst; this increases latency risk for large-context requests.

Attaching workbook. Comments welcome.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: APAC sizing - procurement & cost options

Quick procurement and pricing notes:
- Current lead times for H100 reserved in SIN region: estimated 4–7 weeks (order placed). A100 reserved: 2–4 weeks. If Orbit wants activation in 6 weeks, we need signed MOA and deposit within 72 hours to hit the optimistic timeline.
- Cost tradeoffs (ballpark monthly):
  - 2x H100 reserved + 2x A100 reserved = $78k/mo committed (with 12mo uplift discount).
  - Add warm-standby (4x H100 burst via on-demand) reduces commitment to $78k/mo + on-demand billing during spikes (~$8k per major burst), but keep in mind burst billing is unpredictable.
  - Alternative conservative mix: 4x A100 reserved (no H100) = $64k/mo but expect degraded p95 on heavy context runs; recommend this only if Orbit can tolerate occasional latency degradation or smaller context sizes.

Paperwork items: MOA (commercial terms), SOW (technical scope), and an APAC data processing addendum (DPA) for local logs. I can draft the MOA and the pricing appendix; if we want the 6-week target I need signatures by end of week.

Ben
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: APAC node sizing - initial plan and next steps

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear ask. Quick consolidated recommendation from Redwood:

1) Node mix (recommended, balanced risk/cost):
   - Reserved: 2 x H100 + 2 x A100 in Singapore (reserved capacity to meet baseline and low-latency core).
   - Warm-standby (burst): 4 x H100 on on-demand/hybrid with pre-warmed images and cached KV snapshots.

2) Activation timeline to meet 6-week target:
   - Immediate (0–3 days): sign MOA and SOW; Redwood will place reservation orders and start procurement. (Action: Orbit — execute MOA + initial deposit)
   - Week 1–3: provisioning, kernel tuning for LLM-XX-16B, and cache snapshot seeding. (Action: Redwood infra + Karthik for tuning)
   - Week 4: internal perf canary with synthetic traffic; SLO verification. (Action: Redwood QA)
   - Week 5–6: customer acceptance testing; schedule 2 half-day cutover windows with Orbit. (Action: Orbit + Redwood)

3) Compliance & data residency: logs/KV cache will be retained in-region (Singapore). We'll provide the DPA addendum and an audit checklist. Markus, please share the APAC retention checklist; Maria, this will cover the audit items you flagged.

4) Options if H100 lead time slips: move to the conservative plan (4x A100 reserved + 2x H100 burst) — same activation path but expect higher p95 under aggressive context sizes. We'll include an SLA clause for latency fallback if we need to shift config post-activation.

Attachments: APAC_node_mix_v1.pdf (diagram + cost appendix), sizing-runbook.xlsx (detailed calc), orbitai-moa-draft.pdf (commercial draft).

Next steps:
- Orbit: confirm preferred commitment model (recommended vs conservative) and sign MOA by Fri, 7 Aug to hit 6-week activation.
- Redwood: Ben to share a redlined MOA and cost appendix by EOD Thu.
- Karthik: finalize kernel tuning plan and estimate for cache snapshot tooling.

If you want, we can set a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the diagram.

Cheers,
Neha
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
